# A raise inside a called function reaches the boundary around the handler that
# made the call, on every target, and ends that handler.
#
# Run rather than read, because what is being claimed is what executes: a
# golden shows a recover or a catch, and only running it shows the handler ran
# and the statements after the raise did not. Before passErrorCatch a raise
# that reached a boundary ran its handler and let the click go on, and a raise
# in a call whose value is used (`age = parseTwice("")`) was caught nowhere --
# on the interpreter either, which dispatched only a bare call statement.
#
# The per-call handler is the other half: it catches at its call, the boundary
# never hears of it, and the handler goes on after the statement. The argument
# case holds the line between the two -- a raise from an argument happens
# before the call it is passed to, so it is the boundary's.
#
# Android only compiles the program, in the record of
# testdata/error_raise_through_call.txtar, which declares no test functions.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"

func requireAge(s string) int {
    if s.length == 0 {
        error.raise("an age is required", "validation")
    }
    return int(s)
}

func parseTwice(s string) int {
    var n = requireAge(s)
    return n * 2
}

// One component per case: html's test agent shares one page's state across
// the tests of a component, so two tests of one would each see the other's
// clicks.
component throughCalls node {
    var problem = "none"
    var age = 7
    var after = false
    boundary(@error(e) {
        problem = e.message
    }) {
        button #save(text="Save", @click {
            age = parseTwice("")
            after = true
        })
    }
}

func testRaiseTwoCallsDownReachesBoundary(t Test, c throughCalls) {
    c.save.click()
    t.assert(c.problem == "an age is required")
    t.assert(c.age == 7)
    t.assert(c.after == false)
}

component direct node {
    var problem = "none"
    var after = false
    boundary(@error(e) {
        problem = e.message
    }) {
        button #go(text="Direct", @click {
            error.raise("stop", "")
            after = true
        })
    }
}

func testDirectRaiseEndsHandler(t Test, c direct) {
    c.go.click()
    t.assert(c.problem == "stop")
    t.assert(c.after == false)
}

component perCall node {
    var problem = "none"
    var after = false
    boundary(@error(e) {
        problem = e.message
    }) {
        button #check(text="Check", @click {
            requireAge("", @error(e) {
                problem = "call: " + e.kind
            })
            after = true
        })
    }
}

func testPerCallCatchesAndContinues(t Test, c perCall) {
    c.check.click()
    t.assert(c.problem == "call: validation")
    t.assert(c.after == true)
}

component argument node {
    var problem = "none"
    boundary(@error(e) {
        problem = e.message
    }) {
        button #go(text="Argument", @click {
            parseTwice(string(requireAge("")), @error(e) {
                problem = "not this one"
            })
        })
    }
}

func testRaiseInArgumentReachesBoundary(t Test, c argument) {
    c.go.click()
    t.assert(c.problem == "an age is required")
}

component noRaise node {
    var problem = "none"
    var age = 7
    boundary(@error(e) {
        problem = e.message
    }) {
        button #ok(text="Ok", @click {
            age = parseTwice("21")
        })
    }
}

func testNoRaiseCompletes(t Test, c noRaise) {
    c.ok.click()
    t.assert(c.age == 42)
    t.assert(c.problem == "none")
}

window {
    throughCalls()
    direct()
    perCall()
    argument()
    noRaise()
}
